system.name: OrbitCache
system.one_liner: an in-network key-value cache on programmable switches that serves hot items directly from the data plane

content.subject: how a client detects a hash-collision on a cached key and corrects it via a switch-bypassing round trip to the server

elements.role: issuer of requests; keeps a Requested Key list to detect wrong cached values

elements.role: header of the client's pending-request list, indexed by pkt.seq

elements.role: a pending requested key unrelated to this example

elements.role: another pending requested key unrelated to this example

elements.name: Switch
elements.role: in-network cache that bypasses its cache logic once it detects a correction request

elements.name: Server
elements.role: storage server that holds the authoritative value and answers the correction request

steps.what: client sends a Correction Request (CRN-REQ) after detecting the wrong cached value
switch bypasses its cache logic and forwards the correction request unchanged
storage server returns the correct value as a read reply
switch forwards the read reply back to the client, which removes the key from its list

content.key_idea: When a client detects that the returned key does not match the requested key (a hash collision), it sends a correction request that the switch forwards untouched, bypassing its cache logic, to the storage server, which returns the correct value in a 4-step round trip.
content.reading_order: left to right along the numbered arrows: Client (1) to Switch, (2) to Server, then back (3) Server to Switch, (4) Switch to Client

The switch bypasses the cache logic, and forwards the packet to the server
The client finally gets the correct value for the key DDDD

summary: Figure 6 of OrbitCache walks through how a hash collision in its in-network key-value cache gets corrected. The client's Requested Key list (indexed by pkt.seq) shows it expected DDDD but the reply carried AAAA (annotated top-left as 'From Cache Packet'), so the client marks that pending entry, highlighted in salmon, and in step 1 sends a Correction Request (CRN-REQ) to the switch. In step 2 the switch, now with its cache logic bypassed, forwards CRN-REQ unchanged to the storage server. The server answers with a Read Reply (R-REP) carrying the correct value (step 3), which the switch relays back to the client (step 4), which then removes the key from its list. The four numbered arrows trace this exact correction round trip end to end.
summary_zh: 该图演示OrbitCache处理哈希冲突：客户端发现应答的AAAA与请求的DDDD不符（粉色高亮），发送CRN-REQ给交换机(1)，交换机绕过缓存逻辑转发给服务器(2)，服务器返回正确的R-REP(3)，交换机转发回客户端(4)。
